title: Tutorials
text:
Tutorials (Thursdays 17:00-18:00 in IA 2021) deal with simple astrophysical calculations not discussed in lectures.
If you want a good grade on the written parts of exams and the home assignments, please come to tutorials with some kind of calculating device and practice solving problems.

title: Tutorials
text:
Expectations
Class participation points are given not just for showing up, but for asking/answering questions in class, and volunteering to solve the tutorial problems on blackboard.
As explained in the syllabus, attending tutorials is important for written parts of the exams (half of the points for exams). Tutorials teach you how to approach and numerically solve problems. Many problems are listed and most are fully solved or at least outlined in detail in tutorial notes, which also serve as a preparation material for exams.
Tutorial notes will be posted here as the term progresses.

title: Astrophysics Code & Simulations
text:
This section hosts all computational tools, interactive models, and numerical solvers for ASTB23:

Interactive Galactic Dynamics: In-browser HTML5 Canvas models exploring rotation curve decompositions, disk-halo conspiracies, and dark matter distributions.
Stellar Structure Integrators: Numerical shooting methods and Runge-Kutta ODE solvers for Lane-Emden polytropes (\(n = 1.5, 3.0\)).
Computational Astrophysics Scripts: Python models for H-R diagram synthesis and stellar evolution tracks.

title: ASTB23 Problem Sets & Exams
text:
This section features official assignment problems, step-by-step tutorial guides, and exam preparation packages for ASTB23.

Assignment Submission Protocol
All solutions must be submitted to Quercus by 12:00 noon on due dates. Submissions must be legibly handwritten or typed with: 1. Sketch of physical scenario 2. Analytical derivations 3. Unit verification 4. Plausibility order-of-magnitude checks
